steps.title: Thaw and Plate iPSCs
steps.instruction: Pre‑warm 10 mL Ham’s F12 nutrient mix and mTeSR™ Plus medium to room temperature. Coat 6‑well plates with Geltrex at least 1 h before thawing. Retrieve a cryovial of frozen iPSCs, thaw in a 37 °C water bath (cap kept above water) until only a few ice crystals remain, spray the vial with 70 % ethanol and transfer to a laminar hood. Transfer the cell suspension into a 15 mL Falcon tube containing the pre‑warmed 10 mL Ham’s F12, rinse the vial with 1 mL F12 and add to the tube. Centrifuge 300 × g for 5 min at room temperature, discard supernatant, and gently resuspend the pellet in 2 mL mTeSR™ Plus by pipetting up/down 3–4 times (avoid single‑cell dissociation). Add 2 µL of 1,000× ROCK inhibitor (10 mM Y‑27632) to obtain a final 10 µM concentration. Prepare the Geltrex‑coated 6‑well plate by washing each well with 2 mL DPBS (1×) and aspirating. Add the iPSC suspension to each well (0.5–1 mL per well, distributing 1 cryovial across 1–2 wells) and gently tilt the plate back‑and‑forth to spread cells evenly. Incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ overnight. The next day replace medium with fresh mTeSR™ Plus (no ROCK inhibitor). Change medium daily (2 mL per well) and culture 4–5 days until 70–80 % confluence.

steps.title: Passage iPSCs with ReLeSR
steps.instruction: Prepare new Geltrex‑coated 6‑well plates (coat ≥1 h before use) and pre‑warm mTeSR™ Plus. Aspirate spent medium from confluent iPSC wells and wash once with 2 mL DPBS (without Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺). Add 1 mL ReLeSR to each well, swirl gently, and aspirate after ≤1 min. Add 1 mL mTeSR™ Plus, monitor under a microscope until colonies begin to round at the periphery. Using a cell lifter, detach the aggregates, then pipette the suspension up/down 5–6 times to obtain small clumps. Collect all aggregates into a 15 mL tube, centrifuge 300 × g for 5 min (RT), discard supernatant, and resuspend in 2 mL mTeSR™ Plus. Wash the new plate once with 2 mL PBS to remove residual Geltrex, then add 0.5 mL of the cell suspension to each well and distribute evenly. Add an additional 1.5 mL mTeSR™ Plus (total 2 mL per well) and 2 µL ROCK inhibitor (10 µM final). Perform a 1:4 split ratio (≈80 % confluence) by gently tilting the plate to spread aggregates. Return plate to 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ incubator. Refresh medium daily and monitor until the next passage.

steps.title: Derive MSCs via Direct Plating
steps.instruction: Coat each well of a 6‑well plate with 1 mL 0.1 % gelatin (room temperature, 1 h), then wash once with 1× PBS. Remove mTeSR™ Plus from routine iPSC cultures, wash cells with sterile PBS, add 1 mL ReLeSR per well, swirl, and aspirate after ≤1 min. Add 1 mL mTeSR™ Plus, lift colonies with a cell lifter, and pipette 3–4 times to break colonies into smaller clumps. Collect aggregates into a 15 mL tube, centrifuge 300 × g for 5 min (RT), discard supernatant, wash with 1× PBS, and add 1 mL MSC growth medium. Plate the cell suspension onto the gelatin‑coated wells using a 1:1 or 1:2 split ratio (cells from one well onto one or two new wells) – this is passage 0 (p0). Change MSC growth medium every 2–3 days. After 7–10 days, when a confluent monolayer of flattened and spindle‑shaped cells appears, proceed to the next passage.

steps.title: Expand and Passage iMSCs
steps.instruction: Aspirate medium from confluent iMSC cultures and add 0.5 mL 0.25 % Trypsin‑EDTA per well of a 6‑well dish. Incubate 3–5 min at 37 °C, then gently pipette with a 1 mL pipettor to obtain a single‑cell suspension. Transfer the suspension to a 15 mL tube containing MSC growth medium, centrifuge 300 × g for 5 min (RT), discard supernatant, and resuspend the pellet in MSC growth medium. Count cells and prepare a suspension at 0.25 × 10⁶ cells/mL. Plate 1 mL of this suspension into each gelatin‑coated well (≈0.25 × 10⁶ cells per well) – passage 1 (p1). Maintain at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, changing medium every 2–3 days. When cultures reach ~90 % confluence, detach with 0.25 % Trypsin‑EDTA and reseed at 1 × 10⁴ cells/cm² onto gelatin‑coated plates for routine expansion. Keep track of passage numbers and freeze batches as described below.

steps.title: Cryopreserve iMSCs
steps.instruction: Prepare fresh 2× MSC freezing medium (80 % defined FBS, 10 % MSC growth medium, 10 % DMSO) and keep on ice. Obtain a single‑cell suspension of iMSCs (steps above), count cells and adjust to 2 × 10⁶ cells/mL in MSC growth medium. Mix an equal volume of cold 2× freezing medium with the cell suspension (final 1× freezing medium). Aliquot 1 mL (containing 1 × 10⁶ cells) into each cryogenic vial. Place vials in a controlled‑rate freezing container and store at –80 °C overnight. The following day transfer vials to a –80 °C freezer or liquid‑nitrogen tank for long‑term storage.

steps.title: Flow Cytometry Surface Staining
steps.instruction: Prepare a single‑cell suspension of iMSCs in cold 1 % FBS in DPBS (no Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺) at 2 × 10⁶ cells/mL. Transfer 100 µL (2 × 10⁵ cells) to a 1.5 mL tube. Add the appropriate volume of each MSC antibody (CD34, CD45, CD73, CD90, CD105) as specified in the Antibodies section, mix gently, and incubate 30 min at room temperature in the dark. Wash once with 1 % FBS in DPBS, centrifuge briefly, discard supernatant, and resuspend cells in 250 µL 4 % formaldehyde‑DPBS. Analyze on a flow cytometer.

steps.title: Micromass Chondrogenic Differentiation
steps.instruction: Expand iMSCs in a 10 cm dish in MSC growth medium at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ until 75–80 % confluent. Aspirate medium, wash once with 10 mL PBS, add 1 mL 0.25 % Trypsin‑EDTA, and incubate 3–5 min at 37 °C. Gently pipette to obtain a single‑cell suspension, transfer to a 15 mL tube, centrifuge 300 × g for 5 min (RT), discard supernatant, and resuspend in MSC growth medium. Count cells and dilute to 25 × 10⁶ cells/mL. Spot 10 µL drops (up to three per well) onto the surface of a 6‑well plate; each drop contains 2.5 × 10⁵ cells. Allow cells to attach for 2 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂. Add 1.5 mL MSC growth medium containing 10 µM ROCK inhibitor (Y‑27632) to each well and incubate overnight. After 24 h, replace medium with 2 mL chondrogenic differentiation medium (DMEM‑high glucose, 25 mM HEPES, 100 nM dexamethasone, 50 µg/mL ascorbic acid, 1 % ITS, 40 µg/mL L‑Proline, 1 mM sodium pyruvate, NEAA, GlutaMAX, Pen‑Strep, plus 100 ng/mL BMP‑2 or 10 ng/mL TGF‑β3 added just before use). Continue incubation at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂. On day 2, add fresh chondrogenic medium with BMP‑2 or TGF‑β3. Replace the growth‑factor‑supplemented medium every other day.

steps.title: Pellet Chondrogenic Differentiation
steps.instruction: Harvest iMSCs with 0.25 % Trypsin‑EDTA, centrifuge at 100 × g, and resuspend in MSC growth medium. Count viable cells and aliquot 2.5 × 10⁵ cells in 0.5 mL MSC growth medium into each 15 mL conical tube. Centrifuge 100 × g for 1 min, then incubate tubes overnight at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ with caps loosened for gas exchange. Verify pellet formation after 24–48 h; if pellets do not form, coat tubes with anti‑adherence rinsing solution for 1 h, wash with PBS, and repeat seeding. Replace medium with 0.5 mL chondrogenic differentiation medium supplemented with BMP‑2 (100 ng/mL) or TGF‑β3 (10 ng/mL). Culture pellets for 7, 14, and 21 days, changing medium every other day by gently aspirating the old medium and adding 0.5 mL fresh chondrogenic medium with the appropriate growth factor.

steps.title: Histology of Chondrogenic Pellets
steps.instruction: Harvest pellets, wash once in PBS, and fix in formalin (10 % neutral buffered) for 15 min. Wash twice with PBS. Dehydrate sequentially in 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes: 50 %, 70 %, 95 %, and 100 % ethanol, each for 5 min (repeat the entire series once), then ethanol/xylene, then 100 % xylene (two washes, 5 min each). Embed pellets in low‑melt paraffin, section at 5–7 µm, and mount on Superfrost Plus slides. De‑paraffinize slides in 100 % xylene (two washes, 10 min each), then rehydrate through ethanol series: 100 %, 95 %, 70 %, 50 % ethanol (each 2 min, repeat), followed by distilled water (5 min). Rinse sections in 3 % acetic acid for 3 min. Stain with Alcian Blue at room temperature for 30 min, rinse briefly in acetic acid and tap water, then counterstain with Nuclear Fast Red Kernechtrot for 5 min at RT, rinse in tap water until clear. For Safranin O staining (optional), stain sections in Safranin O solution for 5 min at RT, rinse in tap water (5–10 min), dehydrate through 70 %, 95 %, and 100 % ethanol, then 100 % xylene (two washes, 2 min each), and mount coverslips with CytoSeal mounting medium.

steps.title: qPCR of Cartilage Genes
steps.instruction: Combine 2–3 cell pellets per experimental group with 1 mL TRIzol™ in a 1.5 mL RNase‑free tube. Homogenize by passing the mixture several times through a 26 ½‑gauge needle attached to a 1 mL syringe, vortex, and incubate 5 min at room temperature. Add 200 µL chloroform, vortex 30 s, incubate 5 min, then centrifuge 12,000 × g for 15 min at 4 °C. Transfer the aqueous phase to a new tube, add 500 µL isopropanol, invert to mix, and incubate 30 min at 4 °C (or store at –20 °C). Centrifuge 12,000 × g for 30 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant, and wash the RNA pellet twice with 500 µL 70 % ethanol (5 min spins at 12,000 × g, 4 °C). Air‑dry the pellet, dissolve in nuclease‑free water, and measure concentration with a NanoDrop™. Treat RNA with DNase I per manufacturer’s protocol, then reverse‑transcribe using the High‑Capacity cDNA Reverse Transcription kit. Perform real‑time qPCR with PowerUp SYBR Green Master Mix using gene‑specific primers. Calculate relative expression using the 2⁻ΔΔCt method, normalizing to β‑actin.
